articles.title: High Court Rules Against Hopwood DePree in Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: The High Court has ruled that Rochdale Council acted fairly in its decision not to transfer ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the original owners.
articles.content_html:
A High Court ruling has determined that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision to deny ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the family that originally built the historic property in the 1420s. The ruling concluded a two-day trial held in Manchester, where DePree had challenged the council's decision to terminate an exclusivity agreement for the sale of the Grade II-listed hall.

Following the court's decision, DePree expressed disappointment, stating that it was a significant setback for both his family and the community. He emphasised the importance of Hopwood Hall to local heritage and indicated that his team is exploring further legal options regarding the ruling. DePree also pledged to monitor the council's efforts to preserve and restore the hall for community use.

Hopwood Hall, which is situated within the grounds of Hopwood Hall College, has a rich history, having been owned by the Hopwood family until 1922. After changing hands multiple times, it was acquired by Rochdale Council, which has since been responsible for its upkeep. The hall has suffered from neglect over the years, prompting community interest in its restoration.

The ruling may have implications for future plans regarding the hall's management and restoration. As the council continues to oversee the property, local residents and heritage groups will be keen to see how it addresses the challenges of preserving this significant historical site.
